subject: Chemistry
name: Chemistry, Units 3 and 4
about: VCE, Energy, rates, equilibrium and organic chemistry
syllabus: VCE Chemistry Study Design (from 2023), Units 3 and 4

units.title: Unit 3: How can design and innovation help to optimise chemical processes?

points.title: Fossil fuels and biofuels
points.brief: Coal, natural gas and petrol are fossil fuels; biogas, bioethanol and biodiesel are biofuels that can be replaced quickly by natural processes.

points.title: Energy from food
points.brief: Carbohydrates, proteins and fats are fuels for the body, with energy values measured in kJ per gram.

points.title: Photosynthesis and respiration
points.brief: Photosynthesis stores light energy as glucose; cellular respiration releases it by oxidising glucose back to carbon dioxide and water.

points.title: Making bioethanol
points.brief: Yeast ferments glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide, and distillation concentrates the ethanol for use as fuel.

points.title: Combustion
points.brief: Complete combustion of a fuel gives carbon dioxide and water; incomplete combustion also gives carbon monoxide or soot.

points.title: Limiting reactants
points.brief: The reactant that runs out first sets how much product forms.

points.title: Stoichiometry of fuels
points.brief: Mass, volume and mole ratios find the energy released and the gases made when a fuel burns, at standard conditions.

points.title: Exothermic and endothermic reactions
points.brief: Exothermic reactions release energy (ΔH negative). Endothermic reactions absorb it (ΔH positive).

points.title: Thermochemical equations
points.brief: A balanced equation with ΔH in kJ per mole, which scales with the amounts in the equation.

points.title: Energy profile diagrams
points.brief: Diagrams showing the energy of reactants and products, the activation energy and ΔH.

points.title: Calorimetry
points.brief: Solution calorimetry finds energy changes from temperature changes, using a calibration factor and temperature-time graphs to allow for heat loss.

points.title: Energy content and efficiency
points.brief: Heating water with a burning fuel estimates its energy content. Efficiency is the share of chemical energy that ends up useful.

points.title: Redox and oxidation numbers
points.brief: Oxidation numbers track electrons to identify the oxidising agent, the reducing agent and conjugate redox pairs.

points.title: Half-equations in Unit 3
points.brief: Balanced half-equations, with states, for redox reactions in acidic and basic conditions.

points.title: Galvanic cells
points.brief: Two half-cells joined by a wire and a salt bridge turn chemical energy into electrical energy.

points.title: Anode and cathode
points.brief: Oxidation happens at the anode and reduction at the cathode. In a galvanic cell the anode is negative.

points.title: The electrochemical series
points.brief: A table of half-equations ordered by strength, used to predict which reactions happen and the cell voltage.

points.title: Fuel cells
points.brief: Cells that are fed fuel and oxygen continuously, such as hydrogen fuel cells, making electricity with water as the product.

points.title: Designing better fuel cells
points.brief: Innovation guided by green chemistry, such as energy efficiency and safer materials, is improving fuel cells for society's energy needs.

points.title: Collision theory
points.brief: Particles react when they collide with enough energy and the right orientation.

points.title: Factors affecting rate
points.brief: Higher temperature, concentration, pressure or surface area, and a catalyst, speed up a reaction.

points.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann distributions
points.brief: A graph of particle energies. At higher temperature more particles pass the activation energy.

points.title: Catalysts
points.brief: A catalyst gives a path with lower activation energy and is not used up.

points.title: Reversible reactions and extent
points.brief: Some reactions go both ways. How fast a reaction goes (rate) differs from how far it goes (extent).

points.title: Dynamic equilibrium
points.brief: In a closed system, forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates, so amounts stay constant.

points.title: The equilibrium constant
points.brief: Kc compares product and reactant concentrations at equilibrium. Its value depends on temperature only.

points.title: The reaction quotient
points.brief: Q is worked out like Kc at any moment; comparing Q with Kc shows which way a reaction will shift.

points.title: Le Chatelier's principle
points.brief: A change to an equilibrium shifts it to partly oppose the change, such as adding a reactant making more product.

points.title: Rate and yield in industry
points.brief: Industry chooses conditions that balance a fast rate with a high yield, at reasonable cost.

points.title: Green chemistry principles
points.brief: Designing processes to reduce waste, use safer chemicals, save energy and use renewable feedstocks.

points.title: Electrolysis
points.brief: An external power supply forces a non-spontaneous redox reaction. The electrochemical series predicts the products from molten or aqueous chemicals.

points.title: Commercial electrolytic cells
points.brief: Industrial cells are designed with suitable electrodes and electrolytes, and remove products as they form.

points.title: Rechargeable cells
points.brief: A cell that runs as a galvanic cell when used and as an electrolytic cell when charged.

points.title: Green hydrogen
points.brief: Electrolysis powered by solar or wind, and artificial photosynthesis, can make hydrogen without fossil fuels.

points.title: Faraday's laws
points.brief: The amount of substance made in electrolysis is set by the charge passed, Q = It, and n(e⁻) = Q/F.

units.title: Unit 4: How are carbon-based compounds designed for purpose?

points.title: Why carbon is special
points.brief: Carbon has four valence electrons and forms strong bonds with itself and other atoms, giving millions of compounds.

points.title: Homologous series
points.brief: Families such as alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, amines, amides, carboxylic acids and esters, drawn as molecular, structural, semi-structural or skeletal formulas.

points.title: IUPAC naming
points.brief: Names show the main chain, its functional group, any branches and where each sits.

points.title: Structural isomers
points.brief: Compounds with the same formula but different arrangements of atoms, and so different properties.

points.title: Boiling points of organic compounds
points.brief: Boiling point, melting point and viscosity rise with chain length and with stronger forces between molecules.

points.title: Substitution and addition reactions
points.brief: Alkanes swap a hydrogen for a halogen. Alkenes add atoms across the double bond.

points.title: Esters and amides
points.brief: An alcohol and a carboxylic acid form an ester, and esters can be hydrolysed back. An amine and a carboxylic acid form an amide.

points.title: Reaction pathways
points.brief: A series of reactions makes a target, such as a primary amine or a carboxylic acid, from a simpler compound.

points.title: Making biodiesel
points.brief: Plant oils react with an alcohol in transesterification to make biodiesel.

points.title: Hydrolysis and condensation of biomolecules
points.brief: Condensation builds proteins, starch, glycogen and fats; hydrolysis breaks them down again in digestion.

points.title: Atom economy and yield
points.brief: Percentage yield and atom economy measure how much of the reactants ends up in the product. Green chemistry favours high atom economy.

points.title: Tests for functional groups
points.brief: Simple tests show a carbon-carbon double bond, a hydroxyl group or a carboxyl group.

points.title: Melting point and distillation
points.brief: A sharp melting point shows purity. Simple and fractional distillation separate liquids by boiling point.

points.title: Degree of unsaturation
points.brief: How much iodine a fat or oil absorbs shows how many carbon-carbon double bonds it has.

points.title: Redox titrations
points.brief: Titrating with an oxidising or reducing agent finds a concentration, including which reactant is in excess.

points.title: Mass spectrometry
points.brief: Gives the molecular ion's mass and fragment pattern, which help identify a compound.

points.title: Infrared spectroscopy
points.brief: Bonds absorb particular infrared wavelengths, showing functional groups such as O-H and C=O.

points.title: Proton NMR spectroscopy
points.brief: Shows how many hydrogen environments a molecule has, their surroundings and, by splitting, their neighbours.

points.title: Carbon-13 NMR spectroscopy
points.brief: The number of peaks shows how many different carbon environments there are.

points.title: Chromatography
points.brief: High performance liquid chromatography separates a mixture. Retention times identify parts, and a calibration curve finds concentration.

points.title: Combining techniques
points.brief: Mass spectrometry, infrared and NMR data together reveal the structure of an unknown organic compound.

points.title: Medicines from plants
points.brief: Solvent extraction and distillation take possible active ingredients out of plants and purify them.

points.title: Functional groups in medicines
points.brief: Identifying the functional groups in a medicine's structure shows how it may react and work.

points.title: Chirality in medicines
points.brief: A carbon with four different groups is chiral. Mirror-image forms of a medicine can act very differently in the body.

points.title: Enzymes
points.brief: Proteins that catalyse reactions, with primary to quaternary structure. Heat and pH change their shape and stop them working.

points.title: Enzyme inhibitors
points.brief: Some medicines block an enzyme's active site, so the real substrate cannot bind.

points.title: Variables and controlled experiments
points.brief: Changing one independent variable, measuring the dependent variable and keeping others controlled shows cause and effect.

points.title: Measurement quality in Unit 4
points.brief: Accuracy, precision, repeatability, reproducibility, resolution and validity judge how far results can be trusted.

points.title: Reporting findings
points.brief: A scientific poster or report uses correct terms, units and conventions to present findings and their implications.
